# index

`@amritk/vector` — the package's entry point, the module a Nish program
reaches with `import { … } from "@amritk/vector"`. It holds the command
line (`vectorRun`, which `src/main.ts` calls with the process's arguments)
and the two proofs as functions of JSON text, which read no file and print
nothing.

Generated from [src/index.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/index.ts).

## Exports

- [`VECTOR_VERSION`](#vector_version)
- [`vectorRun`](#vectorrun)
- [`vectorVerifyJson`](#vectorverifyjson)
- [`vectorDiffJson`](#vectordiffjson)

## Declarations

<a id="vector_version"></a>

### VECTOR_VERSION

The version `vector --version` prints; kept equal to package.json's.

```ts
const VECTOR_VERSION: string = "0.1.0"
```

### vectorRun

Runs vector's command line over `args`, as `vector <args>` would: it
prints what the command prints, and `--help`, `--version` and a usage
error end the process, as they do for the binary.

```ts
function vectorRun(args: string[]): i32
```

<scalar-field name="args" type="string[]" required>

the words after the program's name, such as `["verify", "spec.json", "program.json"]`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

the exit code: 0 pass, 1 refused, 2 usage or I/O

</scalar-field>

### vectorVerifyJson

Proves a program meets its spec plan, as `vector verify --json` does, from
the two documents' text rather than their files.

```ts
function vectorVerifyJson(
  specText: string,
  programText: string,
): Result<string, string>
```

<scalar-field name="specText" type="string" required>

the spec plan, as JSON text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="programText" type="string" required>

the program, as JSON text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;string, string&gt;">

`Ok` with the outcome `vector verify --json` prints (its `status`
  is PROVEN, REFUTED, UNKNOWN, INVALID or ERROR), or `Err` when either text
  is not JSON

</scalar-field>

### vectorDiffJson

Proves two versions of a program equivalent, or shows where they differ,
as `vector diff --json` does, from the two documents' text.

```ts
function vectorDiffJson(
  oldText: string,
  newText: string,
): Result<string, string>
```

<scalar-field name="oldText" type="string" required>

the program before, as JSON text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="newText" type="string" required>

the program after, as JSON text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;string, string&gt;">

`Ok` with the outcome `vector diff --json` prints (its `status` is
  EQUIVALENT, DIFFERENT, UNDECIDED, INVALID or ERROR), or `Err` when
  either text is not JSON

</scalar-field>
